title: Module 9: Deeper steel design: columns, LTB, connections and frames
shortTitle: Deeper steel design: columns, LTB, connections and frames
whyItMatters: Real steel structures are 3D assemblages of unrestrained beams, columns under combined axial and eccentric moments, bolted/welded connections, and braced or portal frames where stability and connection stiffness govern the whole model.
introduction: Extends EC3 steel design to unrestrained beams (Lateral Torsional Buckling M_b,Rd = χ_LT·W_pl·f_y/γ_M1, non-dimensional slenderness λ_LT, restraint spacing, load-height effects, web stiffeners), compression members (flexural buckling N_b,Rd = χ·A·f_y/γ_M1, buckling curves a0 to d, beam-column interaction), bolted and welded connections (shear, bearing, tension, block tearing, simple vs moment connections, base plates), and braced vs portal frame stability (second-order P-Δ awareness).
objectives: Follow the EC3 LTB calculation workflow for unrestrained beams and evaluate design alternatives to improve LTB capacity (Project 9.1).
Carry out EC3 column buckling checks using non-dimensional slenderness λ_bar and reduction factor χ, and understand beam-column interaction (Project 9.2).
Understand bolted and welded connection load paths, simple vs moment connection stiffness assumptions, base plates, and braced/portal frame stability (Project 9.3).

questions.learningObjective: Explain why moment gradient affects LTB resistance (C_1 factor)
questions.prompt: Two identical unrestrained beams of length L have the exact same peak bending moment M_max. Beam A has a constant uniform bending moment M_max along its entire length, while Beam B has a moment that varies linearly from +M_max at one end to 0 at the other. Why does Beam B have a significantly higher elastic critical moment M_cr against LTB?
questions.assumptions: Physical explanation of moment gradient factor C_1.
options: Because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel

In Beam A, the entire length of the compression flange is stressed at the peak compressive force simultaneously, whereas in Beam B only one end experiences peak compression while the less-stressed portion of the flange helps restrain lateral buckling

Because the elastic shear modulus G is related to Young’s modulus E by G = E / [2(1 + ν)], which introduces a Poisson’s ratio reduction factor across the web depth whenever transverse direct stresses are neglected in simple beam theory

Because Eurocode partial safety factors for resistance incorporate a statistical log-normal coefficient of variation for hot-rolled plate thickness tolerances, mill rolling residual stresses, and out-of-straightness bow imperfections across the member length
questions.explanation: Uniform compression over the entire unrestrained length (C_1 = 1.0) is the worst case for LTB; a moment gradient leaves most of the flange at lower compression.

questions.prompt: In Syllabus Project 9.1, removing the continuous floor restraint causes your trial Universal Beam to fail in Lateral Torsional Buckling. Which set of design or detailing alternatives would genuinely improve its LTB resistance?
options: Keep the exact same UB and remove the torsional restraints at the end supports, assuming that it redistributes the peak hogging bending moment into the adjacent midspan zone through rigid-plastic hinge rotation without requiring supplementary lateral-torsional restraint, web stiffeners, or ductile rotation capacity at the support interface

Provide intermediate lateral restraints tied to a braced bay (reducing unrestrained length L_LT), or switch to a section with much higher minor-axis stiffness I_z and torsional stiffness J (such as a wider Universal Column UKC section or a closed Rectangular Hollow Section RHS)

It eliminates vertical shear deformation across the web depth by forcing the neutral axis to remain coincident with the geometric centroid of the uncracked transformed section throughout both construction and permanent service stages
questions.explanation: UKC sections have wide flanges (large I_z) and RHS box sections have huge torsional constant J (so RHS beams are virtually immune to LTB at normal spans).

questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose of transverse web stiffeners at supports and heavy point loads
questions.prompt: Why are full-depth transverse steel plates (web stiffeners) welded between the top and bottom flanges on both sides of an I-beam web at heavy column transfer points or unrestrained beam ends?
options: They increase the major-axis second moment of area I_y at midspan by 300%, assuming that the member is verified solely for Ultimate Limit State cross-sectional yield resistance at midspan while relying on friction alone at the bearings to resist horizontal thermal expansion, wind drag, and notional lateral equivalent forces

The structural analysis models the joint as a frictionless pin for vertical gravity load takedown but simultaneously assumes full rotational fixity when evaluating lateral storey drift and global second-order sway stability

The design substitutes the characteristic 95th-percentile material strength in place of the 5th-percentile characteristic strength and omits the combination factor ψ_0 when superimpose-combining independent variable wind and imposed floor actions

They prevent local web crushing and vertical web buckling under concentrated forces, and at beam supports they prevent the top flange from twisting relative to the bottom flange (providing torsional support restraint)
questions.explanation: Load-bearing and torsional stiffeners reinforce the thin web against local out-of-plane buckling and cross-sectional distortion. questions.learningObjective: Explain why EC3 assigns different buckling curves (a0, a, b, c, d) to different sections and axes
questions.prompt: Why does a hot-rolled H-section (UKC) use a more favourable buckling curve (curve "b") for buckling about its major axis y-y than for buckling about its minor axis z-z (curve "c")?
questions.assumptions: Physical reason behind the multiple Perry-Robertson curves in EC3.
options: During cooling after hot rolling, the tips of the flanges cool faster than the web-flange junction, locking in compressive residual stresses at the flange tips; these flange tips lie furthest from the minor axis z-z, causing earlier yielding and greater stiffness loss when buckling about the minor axis

By applying the unfactored characteristic Serviceability Limit State action combination directly to the gross cross-sectional area without accounting for partial material safety factors, second-order geometric imperfections, or local buckling slenderness reductions at the critical section

By assuming a uniform linear-elastic stress distribution across the gross flange and web elements while neglecting rotational restraint compatibility, eccentric shear-centre load introduction, and shear-lag effects at the support boundaries
Because Young’s modulus E is smaller in the flanges than in the web
questions.explanation: Compressive residual stresses at the flange tips reduce the effective minor-axis flexural stiffness I_z much more rapidly than major-axis I_y once compression increases.

questions.prompt: How does the effective buckling length L_cr of a column of storey height L in an unbraced sway frame compare to that of an identical column of storey height L in a braced non-sway frame?
questions.assumptions: Connects column design to global frame stability.
options: Because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel when evaluated under unfactored serviceability actions across the gross cross-section without partial safety factors or second-order geometric slenderness reductions

In a braced frame, horizontal translation of the storey tops is prevented so L_cr ≤ 1.0 L (typically 0.7 L to 1.0 L); in an unbraced sway frame, the top of the column translates sideways during buckling so L_cr > 1.0 L (often 1.5 L to 2.0 L or more), drastically reducing buckling resistance

Because the elastic shear modulus G is related to Young’s modulus E by G = E / [2(1 + ν)], which introduces a Poisson’s ratio reduction factor across the web depth whenever transverse direct stresses are neglected in simple beam theory

Because Eurocode partial safety factors for resistance incorporate a statistical log-normal coefficient of variation for hot-rolled plate thickness tolerances, mill rolling residual stresses, and out-of-straightness bow imperfections across the member length
questions.explanation: Preventing sway via diagonal bracing or shear cores keeps column effective lengths ≤ storey height L. Engineering synthesis for "Compare effective lengths in braced (non-sway) vs unbraced (sway) frames": always trace the complete load path from point of application to the foundations, ensure compatibility between analysis boundary assumptions and physical site detailing, and verify against BS EN 1993-1-1:2005 (Eurocode 3: Member Buckling Resistance, Cl. 6.3.1 & Cl. 6.3.2).

questions.learningObjective: Calculate effective throat thickness a of a symmetric 45° fillet weld

questions.learningObjective: Understand block tearing failure in a bolted beam-end or gusset connection
questions.prompt: What is "block tearing" at a bolted connection (such as a notched beam web or tension gusset plate)?
questions.assumptions: Module 9 Learn item: block tearing awareness.
options: A failure where the concrete foundation cracks 10 m away, assuming that it redistributes the peak hogging bending moment into the adjacent midspan zone through rigid-plastic hinge rotation without requiring supplementary lateral-torsional restraint, web stiffeners, or ductile rotation capacity at the support interface

It increases the elastic Euler critical buckling load by halving the effective buckling length between inflection points, provided that the connection detail transfers full axial thrust without slip or local web crippling

A combined shear-and-tension tear-out failure where a block of plate material rips out along the perimeter of the bolt group, failing simultaneously by shear along the longitudinal bolt row(s) and tension across the transverse end bolt line

It eliminates vertical shear deformation across the web depth by forcing the neutral axis to remain coincident with the geometric centroid of the uncracked transformed section throughout both construction and permanent service stages
questions.explanation: Block tearing is particularly critical when a beam top flange is notched (coped) at a connection, leaving a free top edge above the bolt group. Engineering synthesis for "Understand block tearing failure in a bolted beam-end or gusset connection": always trace the complete load path from point of application to the foundations, ensure compatibility between analysis boundary assumptions and physical site detailing, and verify against BS EN 1993-1-1:2005 (Eurocode 3: Member Buckling Resistance, Cl. 6.3.1 & Cl. 6.3.2).

questions.learningObjective: Understand why connection assumptions affect the whole structural model (Module 9 Gate)
questions.prompt: Suppose an engineer analyses a steel frame assuming beam-to-column joints are frictionless pins (so columns receive zero end moment from the beams), but on the drawings specifies deep, heavily stiffened extended end-plate moment connections welded/bolted to the column flanges. What is the danger of this mismatch?
options: The member is verified solely for Ultimate Limit State cross-sectional yield resistance at midspan while relying on friction alone at the bearings to resist horizontal thermal expansion, wind drag, and notional lateral equivalent forces

The structural analysis models the joint as a frictionless pin for vertical gravity load takedown but simultaneously assumes full rotational fixity when evaluating lateral storey drift and global second-order sway stability

The design substitutes the characteristic 95th-percentile material strength in place of the 5th-percentile characteristic strength and omits the combination factor ψ_0 when superimpose-combining independent variable wind and imposed floor actions

The stiff connections restrain beam end rotation and attract large hogging bending moments into both the connection bolts/welds and the supporting columns, moments that the columns and foundations were never designed to resist
questions.explanation: In structural mechanics, force follows stiffness! If a connection is detailed stiffly, it will attract moment whether the analysis model assumed a pin or not.

questions.learningObjective: Understand why pitched-roof steel portal frames have haunches at the eaves
questions.prompt: In a single-storey pitched-roof steel portal frame, why is the rafter typically deepened with a fabricated haunch at the eaves (beam-to-column knee) connection?
options: Because the largest bending moment in a portal frame occurs at the eaves knee (hogging under gravity load), and deepening the lever arm at the eaves increases bending resistance, increases frame flexural stiffness, and provides room for a multi-row bolted moment end-plate connection

By applying the unfactored characteristic Serviceability Limit State action combination directly to the gross cross-sectional area without accounting for partial material safety factors, second-order geometric imperfections, or local buckling slenderness reductions at the.

By assuming a uniform linear-elastic stress distribution across the gross flange and web elements while neglecting rotational restraint compatibility, eccentric shear-centre load introduction, and shear-lag effects at the support boundaries

By taking the mean 50th-percentile material stiffness modulus together with a fully fixed rotational boundary condition at both ends, thereby ignoring connection flexibility, long-term creep deformation, and differential support settlement under sustained gravity loading
questions.explanation: Note also that under hogging at the eaves haunch, the BOTTOM flange of the haunch is in compression and requires torsional fly-bracing from the purlins/side rails!

questions.learningObjective: Understand second-order (P-Δ) sway effects in frames
questions.prompt: What are "second-order (P-Δ) effects" in a multi-storey or portal steel frame subjected to combined vertical gravity loads P and horizontal wind sway Δ?
options: The effect of painting the steel with a second coat of paint

When the frame sways horizontally by Δ under lateral load, the heavy vertical gravity loads P acting on the displaced nodes create additional overturning moments (P × Δ) that cause further sway and amplify the internal moments and forces beyond first-order elastic analysis

Because the elastic shear modulus G is related to Young’s modulus E by G = E / [2(1 + ν)], which introduces a Poisson’s ratio reduction factor across the web depth whenever transverse direct stresses are neglected in simple beam theory
A reduction in bending moment when axial compression is high
questions.explanation: When a frame is flexible in sway (e.g. α_cr = F_cr / F_Ed < 10 in EC3), second-order P-Δ amplification must be accounted for in the analysis. Engineering synthesis for "Understand second-order (P-Δ) sway effects in frames": always trace the complete load path from point of application to the foundations, ensure compatibility between analysis boundary assumptions and physical site detailing, and verify against BS EN 1993-1-1:2005 (Eurocode 3: Member Buckling Resistance, Cl. 6.3.1 & Cl. 6.3.2).

moduleAssessmentQuestions.learningObjective: Identify how horizontal forces at the base of a portal frame or braced bay are resisted
moduleAssessmentQuestions.prompt: A portal frame column base or a vertical braced bay base exerts a substantial horizontal shear force H_Ed onto its pad foundation. How can this horizontal base reaction be safely resisted in the permanent structure?
moduleAssessmentQuestions.assumptions: Connects Module 9 frames to Module 13 foundations.
options: By assuming horizontal forces disappear once they reach the baseplate, assuming that because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel

By a horizontal steel/concrete tie beam cast into the floor slab connecting opposing column bases (especially in portal frames to resist outward eaves spread thrust), passive earth pressure on the side of the foundation/shear key, and/or base friction under minimum vertical load
By using frictionless PTFE sliding bearings at both bases

Because Eurocode partial safety factors for resistance incorporate a statistical log-normal coefficient of variation for hot-rolled plate thickness tolerances, mill rolling residual stresses, and out-of-straightness bow imperfections across the member length
moduleAssessmentQuestions.explanation: Pitched-roof portal frames push outwards at the bases under gravity load; tying the bases together across the floor slab is standard UK practice to avoid large horizontal foundation thrusts.

moduleAssessmentQuestions.learningObjective: Synthesise the Module 9 Learning Gate on global stability and connection assumptions
moduleAssessmentQuestions.prompt: When reviewing a 3D steel frame design, which four questions form the Module 9 Learning Gate check?
moduleAssessmentQuestions.assumptions: Module 9 Gate synthesis.
options: It redistributes the peak hogging bending moment into the adjacent midspan zone through rigid-plastic hinge rotation without requiring supplementary lateral-torsional restraint, web stiffeners, or ductile rotation capacity at the support interface when evaluated under unfactored serviceability actions across the gross cross-section without partial safety factors or second-order geometric slenderness reductions

It increases the elastic Euler critical buckling load by halving the effective buckling length between inflection points, provided that the connection detail transfers full axial thrust without slip or local web crippling

(1) Are unrestrained beams checked for LTB rather than just cross-section strength? (2) Are columns checked for flexural/torsional buckling and eccentric moments rather than just squash load? (3) Is there a complete, credible 3D lateral stability system (diaphragms + vertical bracing/moment frames) in both permanent and erection stages? (4) Do the physical connection details match the pinned or rigid stiffness assumptions of the analysis model?

It eliminates vertical shear deformation across the web depth by forcing the neutral axis to remain coincident with the geometric centroid of the uncracked transformed section throughout both construction and permanent service stages
moduleAssessmentQuestions.explanation: Summarises all four pillars of the Module 9 Learning Gate. Engineering synthesis for "Synthesise the Module 9 Learning Gate on global stability and connection assumptions": always trace the complete load path from point of application to the foundations, ensure compatibility between analysis boundary assumptions and physical site detailing, and verify against BS EN 1993-1-1:2005 (Eurocode 3: Member Buckling Resistance, Cl. 6.3.1 & Cl. 6.3.2).
